description: Terrestrial laser scans of the Port Hills Rockfall from the Canterbury New Zealand Earthquake Sequence is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Chris Massey, GNS Science (gns.cri.nz). Several rockfalls occurred during and following the Canterbury New Zealand Earthquake Sequence. GNS Science collected repeat terrestrial lidar scans of large rockslopes to quantify rockfall volumes and track changes throughout the sequence. Coverage: Christchurch, New Zealand. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Rockfall, earhquake, Port Hills, terrestrial lidar, terrestrial laser scanning. Published 2021-12-14. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
